newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended higher, but could not hold on to the peaks reached during the session when March Bund futures crossed the crucial 104.00 level.
Dealers said volumes were thin around lunchtime, making it easier for the Bund future to rise to its intraday high.
"Maybe it's because there are no figures, no impulses, there are just no barriers left," one dealer said.
Cash trade was minimal and dominated by professional traders, focusing on the new February 2007 state loan and the long benchmark, while turnover in futures was far above average, dealers said.
The February 2007 benchmark gained 0.14 points to 102.96/103.04, for a bid yield of 5.36 pct. The January 2023s ended 0.35 points higher at 118.70/90, for a 6.05 percent bid yield.

"The market in itself doesn't do very much, traders hold to their positions as long as (the direction of) interest rates doesn't change. We're just adjusting our screen prices to what's happening in the futures," one dealer said.
Lengthening of positions continued, dealers said, although they noted some parties started to reduce their holdings.

"It's a matter of gravity, everything that goes up ends by going down. I think the number of bears is on the increase," one dealer said, adding he would not be surprised if the March Bund future headed back to 102.30 within a couple of days.
